name: MonarchCursorList
title: CursorList
wrapsNative: List with .listStyle(.plain) and a MonarchLoadMore footer row; MonarchErrorState, MonarchLoadingState and MonarchEmptyState for the first-load states; accessibilityFocused(_:equals:) for the first new item
summary: A list loaded page by page from a cursor: the items, a load-more footer with a count, and the first-load, empty and error states.
whenToUse: For a screen or tab whose content is a long list fetched in pages from an API cursor (requests, activity, messages), when the app keeps the cursor in its model.
whenNotToUse: For a list loaded whole, use a List. For rows with several columns, use MonarchDataTable with a MonarchLoadMore footer. Inside another scroll view, use MonarchLoadMore under a LazyVStack instead, because a List does not size to its content.
api: init(_ items: [Item], label: String, hasMore: Bool, isLoading: Bool = false, isFailed: Bool = false, totalCount: Int? = nil, autoLoads: Bool = false, showsEnd: Bool = true, isDivided: Bool = true, focusesNewItems: Bool = true, loadingVariant: MonarchLoadingStateVariant = .list, labels: MonarchCursorListLabels = MonarchCursorListLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onLoadMore: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void, @ViewBuilder row: @escaping (Item) -> Row) where Item: Identifiable
struct MonarchCursorListLabels { var loading, emptyTitle, emptyMessage, errorTitle, retry: String?; var footer: MonarchLoadMoreLabels }

options.name: items
options.description: Every item loaded so far, in order.

options.name: hasMore
options.description: Whether there is another page. With no items and no more, shows the empty state.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: A page is being fetched. With no items, shows the loading state; otherwise the footer button shows progress.

options.name: isFailed
options.description: The last fetch failed. With no items, shows the error state; otherwise the footer shows the failure with retry.

options.name: totalCount
options.description: The total, when the server knows it, for "Showing 20 of 140 items".

options.name: autoLoads
options.description: Loads the next page when the footer scrolls into view; the button stays as the fallback.

options.name: showsEnd
options.description: Whether "That's everything" is shown after the last page.

options.name: isDivided
options.description: Whether rows are separated by the list's lines.

options.name: focusesNewItems
options.description: Moves VoiceOver focus to the first item of a page asked for from the footer.

options.name: loadingVariant
options.description: The shape of the first-page placeholder.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the footer's.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Repeats the failed request. By default onLoadMore.

states.name: ready
states.description: The items and the footer: a Load more button with the count, or the end line.

states.name: failed later
states.description: The footer shows "Couldn't load more." with Retry; the items stay.

states.name: first page failed
states.description: A MonarchErrorState, "This list could not be loaded", with Retry; while the retry runs the button is busy.

states.name: empty
states.description: A MonarchEmptyState, "Nothing here yet" with a message.

appearance: A plain list with a hidden background, so it sits on the screen's background; separators are the system's. The footer count and end line are caption text in the muted role; the states use their components' roles. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: The web CursorList chooses ul or ol and takes an item class; on iOS it is a List and the row closure draws each item. The web moves keyboard focus to the first new item after a page asked for by keyboard; on iOS VoiceOver focus moves to it after a page asked for from the footer. The web replaces the empty state with any node; on iOS the empty title and message are labels. The web count noun is built into its messages; on iOS pass labels.footer.count and labels.footer.loaded. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The list is named by label.
The footer is a MonarchLoadMore: its button is a standard button with a 44-point touch target, and new items, a failure and the end are announced.
After a page asked for from the footer arrives, VoiceOver focus moves to its first item.
The first-load placeholder, error and empty states are the shared Monarch states with their own labels.
edgeCases: With no items but more to load and no fetch running, the list shows only the footer, so the first page can be asked for.
A failure with items keeps them and shows the footer failure, not the error state.
A page that brings no new items moves no focus.
The list fills the space it is given; give it a frame when it sits in a stack.

examples.title: With useLoadMore and a server-rendered first page
examples.webExample: With useLoadMore and a server-rendered first page
examples.template:
MonarchCursorList(
    requests,
    label: {{label}},
    hasMore: true,
    totalCount: {{total}},
    labels: MonarchCursorListLabels(footer: MonarchLoadMoreLabels(count: { loaded, total in
        "Showing \(loaded) of \(total ?? loaded) " + (total == 1 ? {{noun.one}} : {{noun.other}})
    })),
    onLoadMore: {},
    row: { request in
        HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline, spacing: MonarchTokens.Space.space3) {
            Text(request.method)
                .monarchTextStyle(.code)
                .foregroundStyle(theme.colors.textMuted)
            Text(request.path)
                .monarchTextStyle(.code)
            Spacer()
            Text(String(request.status))
                .monarchTextStyle(.body)
                .foregroundStyle(request.status >= 400 ? theme.colors.dangerStrong : theme.colors.textMuted)
        }
    }
)
.frame(height: 620)
